happeningTypes.name: Reflect and write about a personally important value
happeningTypes.description: Invite a consenting participant to select and explain a personally important value in a specified writing task. Not generic praise, group superiority, efficacy, trait change or practitioner permission.
happeningTypes.constraints: Voluntary participation, privacy of value disclosures, distress safeguards, accessibility and context-specific ethical assessment; no automatic clinical use.

happeningTypes.name: Voluntarily write a specified counterattitudinal statement under a declared choice protocol
happeningTypes.description: Ask a consenting participant to write a statement inconsistent with a previously specified attitude under declared choice conditions. Operation does not guarantee discomfort, attitude change or real-world persuasion.
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, freedom to decline, debriefing, no coercion or harmful dissemination; manipulation/compliance and private versus public delivery must be explicit.

happeningTypes.name: Recall and describe an experienced shared crisis within a specified research task
happeningTypes.description: Invite a consenting participant to recall and describe a specified previously experienced collective crisis. This does not create a crisis, induce trauma deliberately, guarantee fusion or imply recommendation.
happeningTypes.constraints: Trauma-sensitive consent, option to decline, distress support, privacy and contextual ethics review. No practitioner recommendation or manipulation of real group loyalty.

assertions.scope: Important personal-value reflection in studied individual writing protocols; not group praise or pride-recall equivalence.
assertions.measurement: Self-compassion, health-message acceptance and wellbeing outcomes do not directly identify global self-integrity threat.
assertions.timing: Immediate task evidence; enduring change and recovery not established.
assertions.mechanism: Potential broadening of valued self-resources; downstream acceptance does not identify causal threat reduction.
assertions.risk: Convenience samples, bundled manipulation, demand/measurement effects, privacy and distress; no recommendation or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Benefits on other outcomes and heterogeneous synthesis do not directly establish exact threat change; different affirmation operations must not be pooled as one efficacy estimate.

assertions.scope: Private counterattitudinal writing under high/free choice versus low/instructed choice in two laboratory experiments without aversive consequences.
assertions.measurement: Reported negative discomfort is closer to experienced dissonance than preference spreading, but exact measure/protocol and independent replication require extraction.
assertions.timing: Immediate task evidence; enduring change and recovery not established.
assertions.mechanism: Perceived inconsistency/choice responsibility may produce discomfort; no universal discomfort from logical inconsistency.
assertions.risk: Convenience samples, bundled manipulation, demand/measurement effects, privacy and distress; no recommendation or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Bounded experimentally elicited discomfort is plausible, but abstract/selected passage access and exact measurement/replication limits keep claim research-needed; preference-spreading artifact does not invalidate all discomfort experiments.

assertions.scope: Recall of toughest COVID months versus last journey to work/school among Spanish undergraduates; immediate country-fusion questionnaire only.
assertions.measurement: Seven-item country-fusion score immediately after recall does not establish enduring visceral oneness at canonical weeks/months-years scale.
assertions.timing: Immediate task evidence; enduring change and recovery not established.
assertions.mechanism: Shared-experience recall might temporarily change reported oneness; mechanism and persistence not identified.
assertions.risk: Convenience samples, bundled manipulation, demand/measurement effects, privacy and distress; no recommendation or model eligibility.
assertions.rationale: Published result summaries contain an unresolved F/statistic versus means/SD consistency issue. Preserve reported qualitative result, no quantitative estimate adopted; time-scale mismatch independently prevents readiness.

findings.measurement: Self-perception, wellbeing, social and psychological-barrier outcomes
findings.result: Small average benefits across four outcome classes; interventions/outcomes heterogeneous.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE exact global-threat direct measurement; review/primary overlaps not independent replication; no protocol-wide efficacy.

findings.population: Study participants in brief writing experiments
findings.context: Study participants in brief writing experiments
findings.result: Important-value writing increased self-compassion; ancillary outcome/mechanism contrasts reported.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE direct PSY-100 threat target; self-compassion is not global threat, no independently identified mediation or enduring change.

findings.sample: 592 randomized/563 final per abstract; discussion says591, discrepancy retained
findings.comparator: Control task with factorial efficacy-information condition
findings.measurement: Acceptance of risk information, condom taking and HIV testing
findings.result: No detected effects on the listed outcomes, including with efficacy information.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE exact values-writing identity and global-threat measure. Nondetection is not equivalence; population/culture and operation distinctions retained.

findings.measurement: Defensive processing/ingroup bias and other group responses
findings.result: Near-zero heterogeneous aggregate; group values and positive characteristics show different outcome patterns.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE individual personal-value identity. No equivalence from average nondetection; group and individual operations not interchangeable.

findings.sample: E1 initial23 including noncompliance analysis; E2 exact N not extracted
findings.exposure: High/free-choice private counterattitudinal statement without aversive consequences
findings.timing: After writing; E2 later attitude measure
findings.result: High-choice condition reported more negative discomfort; E2 discomfort reduced after attitude change.
findings.limitations: Selected passages not complete methods. Exact items, full protocol/compliance and replication needed; temporal association of relief and attitude change does not establish a pathway.

findings.design: Mathematical identification analysis with experimental control
findings.result: Apparent spreading can arise without actual attitude change under specified measurement/selection conditions.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE direct experienced-discomfort target and counterattitudinal-writing identity. Mathematical result is not empirical proof all dissonance is absent; empirical component not independent theorem replication.

findings.exposure: Recall toughest COVID months and describe feelings
findings.result: Article reports higher fusion after crisis recall; F/statistic versus means/SD summaries are internally inconsistent.
findings.limitations: No quantitative estimate adopted pending source reconciliation; immediate score not enduring canonical change. Posthoc interpersonal versus intrapersonal coding not randomized mediator.

findings.population: Different sampled respondents across time in Spain/Ukraine
findings.context: Different sampled respondents across time in Spain/Ukraine
findings.result: Initial group-level elevations later subsided; surveys do not follow the same persons.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE randomized recall identity; between-wave composition/confounds cannot identify within-person enduring effects.

findings.design: Mathematical evolutionary model with separate empirical studies
findings.sample: Model plus multiple specialized empirical samples
findings.population: Distinct study populations, not one common experiment
findings.context: Distinct study populations, not one common experiment
findings.exposure: Shared experience/kinship mechanisms in theory and varied tasks
findings.result: Model and empirical results motivate shared-experience/fusion hypotheses; they do not establish one enduring crisis-recall causal effect.
findings.limitations: Model component explicitly not empirical observation. Other-person/shared-event and group-fusion constructs differ; no reachability-to-mediation inference or independent review/study replication.
